subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Should Microsoft Teams file-consent uploads adopt a fixed five-minute whole-request deadline even though very slow valid transfers previously had no cutoff?
rationale: Source, tests, and real HTTP output establish that cancellation works, but repository evidence does not define a minimum supported transfer rate that makes five minutes unconditionally compatible across configurable payload sizes.

options.title: Accept five minutes
options.body: Land the current patch and explicitly own the rare case where a very slow valid upload aborts and must be retried through consent.

options.title: Use a payload-safe bound
options.body: Increase or derive the internal deadline from the supported media-size envelope and a documented minimum transfer rate before merge.

options.title: Decline a whole-request cutoff
options.body: Keep current behavior until an inactivity-based timeout or stronger Microsoft transfer contract can bound stalls without capping healthy transfer duration.

recommendation.title: Accept five minutes
recommendation.body: Land the current patch and explicitly own the rare case where a very slow valid upload aborts and must be retried through consent.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged commits introduced and connected the consent upload execution path whose compatibility behavior changes here.
